newsitem.title: UK: Clyde defends valuation method. [CORRECTED 18:55 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Clyde defends valuation method. [CORRECTED 18:55 GMT]

text.p: Clyde Petroleum Plc defended its use of cash flow multiples to value itself following an attack from hostile bidder Gulf Canada Resources Ltd .

Earlier, Gulf Canada accused the British company of using "unprecedented" methodology in its defence document published on Sunday. Clyde claimed that Gulf Canada's 432 million stg offer put its on a cash flow multiple of 5.7 times compared with 8.9 times for internationally comparable companies.
In an increasingly bitter war of words between the two sides over methods used to value the British company, group managing director Roy Franklin said Gulf Canada's attack was "ironic."
"From the first day of the bid it was clear that what Gulf Canada coveted in Clyde was our strong cash flow," he said.
(Corrects Franklin's quote to "...cash flow..." from "...cash flow multiple.")

He said Gulf Canada's claim that net asset valuation was the only method used by British analysts was "nonsense," and added that Clyde's strong cash flow and developing production base made it "directly comparable to our North American peers" which are usually judged on a cash flow basis.

The managing director declined to be drawn on recent contacts with shareholders, but said "the offer on the table is 105 pence, and the unequivocal recommendation to our shareholders is that an independent Clyde will deliver far greater value."
